checks: For a proper planar cap, an interior point on its cutting plane sees a nonempty open hemisphere of directions toward the positive side. Radial projection of the corresponding boundary patch onto the circle is Lipschitz, so this patch has positive boundary length.

The positive margin hinge is nonnegative and convex, vanishes outside that cap, and therefore pays at least its profile weight. Two weights yield at least 1/2, while each weight of a three-row profile with all weights below 4/9 is above 1/9. Every pair then has sum above 5/9.

The unique exposing maximum in the convex hull of finitely many compact lifted fibers must belong to the original measured union, since each point in a maximizing convex representation is a maximizer.

Strict double capture and compactness localize a sufficiently shallow affine hinge entirely inside both caps on the measured support. The exposed point is on its own fiber boundary and an open neighborhood there has positive surface measure, so the denominator is positive.
The argument applies to an exposed point as stated and makes no assumption that every extreme point is exposed.

overlap.comparison: The accepted result supplies a global exposing affine functional for certain sampled boundary points under strict compatibility. It does not give the strict double-intersection payment, and this frozen proof assumes its own exposed point directly.

readability: The statement and proof are readable as written.
review_method: independent cold proof read of the frozen candidate, original-source and pinned-predecessor comparison, and exact arithmetic where applicable
summary: Both positive-margin localization tests have positive actual boundary denominator and the claimed planar payment.
